cautions.label: C1 Spec Kit on non-roadmap load

caution.finding: On legacy modules with no reachable owner, Spec Kit has been observed fabricating constitution mandates, inventing performance budgets, and tightening schemas in ways that break against existing data.
caution.mitigation: Bound Spec Kit to architecturally novel work. Require a measured baseline before any performance claim. Review every schema change against production data shape.

cautions.label: C2 constitution.md is not a control

caution.finding: constitution.md is prompt context, not a control. Nothing outside the agent re-reads it or blocks a violating change. It will not satisfy an auditor asking what prevents a violation.
caution.mitigation: Pair with overlay F. Treat the constitution as documentation of intent and CI as the enforcement. If segregation of duties must be provable, prefer Spec Kitty's lane state machine.

cautions.label: C3 Superpowers under a metered budget

caution.finding: Superpowers' full loop is token-intensive by design; users under metered plans report slowdowns and reversion. Setup runs 10–20 minutes per feature.
caution.mitigation: Adopt TDD and code-review skills selectively rather than the full mandatory progression. Reserve brainstorming for genuinely ambiguous work.
caution.source: Superpowers release notes and field reports; §8.6

caution.finding: The source material recommends Tessl [@test] anchors as fail-closed verification. They are not: check-spec-links.sh verifies that links point to existing files. The tile is watch-status and stale.
caution.mitigation: Use Superpowers' TDD iron law. Borrow Tessl's one-question-at-a-time interview discipline without adopting the tile.

cautions.label: C5 OpenSpec verify does not block archive

caution.finding: /opsx:verify exists only in the expanded profile and must be configured explicitly. Even then it flags issues without blocking archiving.
caution.mitigation: Run openspec config profile to enable expanded. Add overlay F so the actual gate is CI.

caution.finding: Spec Kitty's lane machine permits exactly 27 transitions and requires implementation evidence to reach for_review; overrides demand actor and reason. This is a stronger audit artifact than Markdown-based governance.
caution.mitigation: Treat Spec Kitty's status log as an audit record. Protect append-only log merges in review — conflict resolution can lose events.

caution.finding: Per-change ceremony dominates at high change volume. Field measurement puts Spec Kit at roughly one full session per ~2,000 LOC unit.
caution.mitigation: Adopt overlay G's two-track policy and hold the heavyweight pipeline for architecturally novel work only.

cautions.label: C8 Spec Kitty below three workers

caution.finding: Spec Kitty's worktree model pays off through concurrency. Below three concurrent workers it adds sync and rebase friction without the benefit. Isolation is partial: full checkouts with ownership metadata.
caution.mitigation: Use plain git worktrees or Superpowers' using-git-worktrees skill instead of Spec Kitty's full mission model.

caution.finding: Created 2026-05-22 — roughly four months old at the evidence date. Release cadence is high but there is little track record, and .planning/ is still evolving.
caution.mitigation: Pin a version. Budget for migration between minor releases. Re-verify activity before committing a team to it.

caution.finding: No commits on main in the 30 days before the evidence date (v6.3.0, 2026-08-12), while comparable projects posted 100+. Star count reflects historical popularity.
caution.mitigation: Check current repository activity before adopting. The methodology is portable, so a pause is survivable — do not assume active upstream support.

caution.finding: The GitHub API reports a non-standard license (NOASSERTION) where comparable projects are MIT.
caution.mitigation: Have legal review the license terms before enterprise adoption.

caution.finding: Interrupt-driven work arrives in real time. Spec Kit, Superpowers' mandatory progression, and BMAD's full method price a session per change that the queue will not wait for.
caution.mitigation: Prefer OpenSpec (or BMAD Quick Flow if BMAD is already the base) as the daily path. Do not run the full Spec Kit or Superpowers pipeline on interrupt tickets.

caution.finding: Core delivery waits on an external vendor release train. No SDD framework removes that blocker.
caution.mitigation: Keep the selected stack for work this team owns. Treat vendor-gated work as out of scope for the SDD recommendation rather than overlaying Spec Kitty.
